subject: FinTechCo RTBF / deletion workflow - next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Higgins <tom.higgins@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechCo RTBF / deletion workflow - next steps

Hi Tom — great to meet on the call today, thanks for walking through FinTechCo's data handling needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: \n\n1) Scope of PII: you confirmed the record types we discussed (user profile PII, payment tokens, and full-text transcripts tied to user IDs). Please flag if I missed anything.\n2) Deletion trigger: you want the ability to submit RTBF/delete requests via API or a ticketing flow with an SLA.\n3) Backups & snapshots: you asked about purging data from backups and whether we can guarantee a maximum purge timeline.\n4) Logging & audit: you need an auditable deletion report that shows the request, actions taken, and final purge confirmation.\n5) Data residency: EU customers must remain within EU regions; would like confirmation our deletion applies across regional replicas.\n\nNext steps for us:\n- Can you share a sample deletion request format (we can support either API payload or a CSV/Doc template)?\n- We'll pull together our standard RTBF playbook and a retention table showing live store vs backups vs logs (attaching a draft).\n- I'll loop in Lauren (legal) and Rishi (engineering) to confirm backup purge constraints and any contractual language you may need.\n\nAttachments: RTBF_playbook.pdf (draft), Redwood_data-retention-table.xlsx (draft)\n\nHappy to sync again next week — what does your availability look like Tue/Wed?\n\nBest,\nCamila Reyes\nAccount Executive, Redwood Inference\ncamila@redwood.ai\n+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Tom Higgins <tom.higgins@fintechco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Data Privacy <data-privacy@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: FinTechCo RTBF / deletion workflow - next steps

On Fri, Mar 20, 2026 at 3:08 PM Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Tom — great to meet on the call today, thanks for walking through FinTechCo's data handling needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: \n> \n> 1) Scope of PII: you confirmed the record types we discussed (user profile PII, payment tokens, and full-text transcripts tied to user IDs). Please flag if I missed anything.\n
Thanks Camila — that summary is accurate. A couple clarifications from our side:\n\n- Deletion SLA: for end-user initiated RTBF we need confirmation that data in live stores is removed within 72 hours.\n- Backups: acceptable purge window for us is 30 days (we prefer aggressive purge but recognize some snapshot policies may extend that). We need an explicit statement about whether backups are overwritten or retained as immutable snapshots.\n- Audit log: the deletion report should include request timestamp, actor, affected object IDs, and final purge timestamp. Ideally available as an export (CSV/PDF) for our auditors.\n- Residency: EU-citizen data must be deleted from EU regions only; we have separate non-EU cohorts.\n\nAttaching FinTechCo's deletion request template for reference (see attachment). Let us know if you can support API or if we'll use the template + ticketing.\n\nThanks,\nTom\nTom Higgins\nHead of Data Privacy, FinTechCo\ntom.higgins@fintechco.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Higgins <tom.higgins@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo RTBF / deletion workflow - next steps

Thanks Tom — appreciate the concrete asks and template. Looping in Lauren (legal) and Rishi (engineering) to confirm specifics and provide timelines we can commit to. Quick notes from product/engineering perspective (preliminary):\n\n- API + Console: Redwood supports both an authenticated DELETE API and a console-driven request flow. We can accept the template you sent via ticketing and map fields to the API payload.\n- Live-store purge: standard flow is to mark records for deletion immediately and remove them from primary stores within 24-72 hours depending on in-flight requests; we can commit to 72 hours SLA for live stores.\n- Backups/snapshots: backups are managed as daily snapshots. Typical purge policy is 30-90 days depending on the customer's retention tier. For FinTechCo we can offer a 30-day backup purge policy as an enterprise config for Hosted accounts; for Dedicated/Private deployments we will need to confirm with ops (see note below).\n- Audit/export: we can provide a deletion report (CSV export) including request ID, actor, affected object IDs, action timestamps, and final purge confirmation. Logs are retained by default for 180 days; shorter retention is available via contract for enterprise plans.\n- Data residency: deletion requests will propagate to regional replicas; for EU-only cohorts we'll ensure actions occur only within EU region datasets.\n\nCaveats & items for legal: \n- Backups: permanent deletion from immutable offsite backups may be constrained by third-party snapshot retention policies and cloud-provider backup windows — Lauren, can you comment on contractual language / exceptions?\n- Regulatory holds: if FinTechCo has legal/regulatory retention obligations for specific records, we'll need a documented hold process.\n\nAttachments: RTBF_playbook.pdf, Redwood_data-retention-table.xlsx\nRelated HubSpot: https://redwood.app/hubspot/contacts/12345\n\nNext step: Lauren/Rishi — can you confirm (1) contractual wording for a 30-day backup purge exception, (2) confirmation that 72-hour live-store SLA is acceptable to legal/ops, and (3) whether we can produce a per-request deletion report export? If yes, I'll propose a short follow-up call with Tom to finalize operational SLAs and any contract language.\n\nThanks — Camila\n\nCamila Reyes\nAccount Executive, Redwood Inference\n

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Tom Higgins <tom.higgins@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo RTBF / deletion workflow - next steps
\nThanks Camila / Tom — quick note from legal:\n\n- 72-hour live-store deletion SLA is acceptable. We'll include language in the SOW specifying "removal from live production stores within 72 hours of a validated RTBF request."\n- Backups: we can offer a contractual backup purge commitment of 30 days for Hosted customers, with an explicit exception for snapshot immutability during provider restore windows. We will add a clause that describes the backup purge as a best-effort within 30 calendar days, with notification to the customer if longer retention applies due to third-party provider constraints.\n- Audit/export: we can commit to providing a per-request deletion report (CSV) containing the fields Tom requested. We'll include that as a deliverable in the implementation checklist.\n- Regulatory holds: we'll ensure a documented process for holds; if a hold is asserted, deletion will be paused and the customer notified with steps to lift the hold.\n\nRishi — can you prepare a short ops note describing the deletion flow (live store vs backup, expected timelines, and any region-specific caveats) so Camila and I can share with Tom on the follow-up call?\n\nI'll be available Wed 10-11am PT or Thu 2-3pm PT for a joint call with FinTechCo.\n\nLauren Bishop\nSenior Counsel (Data + Privacy), Redwood Inference
